slot.brief: Assign R/S to two or three Fischer projections of the same stereocentre; identify identical/enantiomeric pairs or rank by configuration.

stem: Three Fischer projections have the same four groups at a stereocentre; vertical bonds point away and horizontal bonds point towards the viewer. I: top $\text{COOH}$, bottom $\text{CH}_3$, left $\text{OH}$, right $\text{H}$; II: top $\text{COOH}$, bottom $\text{CH}_3$, left $\text{H}$, right $\text{OH}$; III: top $\text{CH}_3$, bottom $\text{COOH}$, left $\text{OH}$, right $\text{H}$. Which pair represents identical configurations?

verdicts.working: Priorities are OH > COOH > CH₃ > H. II differs from I by swapping OH and H; III differs from I by swapping COOH and CH₃. Each is one swap, so II and III have the same configuration.

working:
Priority: $	ext{OH} > 	ext{COOH} > 	ext{CH}_3 > 	ext{H}$.
I: lowest priority is horizontal; inversion gives $S$.
II: lowest priority is horizontal; inversion gives $R$.
III: lowest priority is horizontal; inversion gives $R$.
Thus II and III are identical.

Independent check: Priorities are OH > COOH > CH₃ > H. II differs from I by swapping OH and H; III differs from I by swapping COOH and CH₃. Each is one swap, so II and III have the same configuration.
solution:
Priority order is $\text{OH} > \text{COOH} > \text{CH}_3 > \text{H}$. Since the lowest-priority group is horizontal in each projection, reverse the apparent order of $1\to2\to3$.
I is $S$, while II and III are both $R$; hence II and III have identical configurations.
